text: Hear that? Those are my cousins! The spring peepers!
Spring peepers are tiny frogs. On spring nights, they sing all together, so loudly you can hear them from far away.
Look up, Sprout. What do you see?
A nest, with birds asleep in it. And a squirrel, curled up in a hole in the trunk. And little moths on the bark.
And down below, its roots hold the soil together, all around my tunnels.
And its leaves blow into my pond, and make cozy places for bugs!
And I rest on its branches when the night is long.
An old oak tree can be home to hundreds of different kinds of creatures. Birds and squirrels, moths and beetles, and many more.
So the old oak was never by itself at all.
Never. It looks after all of them. And they look after it, too.
The jays and squirrels bury its acorns all over the meadow. And some of the acorns they forget grow into new oak trees.
It's true. Jays and squirrels hide acorns to eat later. And the ones they never come back for can grow into new oaks.
So maybe... a squirrel planted me?
The old oak isn't a squirrel, or a bird, or a frog. But they all belong with it.
That's my secret. You don't have to be the same as your friends. You just look after each other.
